//: c8 coverage config - WEB baseline. Enforces the >=85% bar on the UNIT-TESTABLE LOGIC LAYER only (pure logic in src/lib + adapters' pure paths). Philosophy: coverage thresholds apply to logic you CAN unit-test, not to I/O glue that genuinely needs live services. That glue is excluded from the denominator and verified by integration tests + a production build instead. Excluding it is NOT gaming coverage: each excluded file must be a thin adapter whose PURE decision half lives in a separate, tested sibling module.
//exclusion-rule: The rule for adding a file to `exclude`: it must be a THIN adapter (DB/network/FS/socket/crypto client, worker orchestration, or a Next.js request-surface guard) whose decision half already lives in a tested pure sibling (a *-policy / *-shape / *-plan / *-rules module). If a file has branching logic and no pure sibling, DO NOT exclude it: extract the pure half and test it.
//exclusion-categories: Categories seen in practice (adapt to your repo): db-stores (raw Drizzle/pg CRUD, covered by *.integration.test.ts against a real DB); network-fetchers (fetch/HTTP clients, ok/!ok fallbacks only, shaping lives in *-shape siblings); worker-glue (multi-step orchestrators, scheduling decisions are pure in *-plan siblings); request-surface (server-only guards touching next/navigation | next/server | auth); adapter-ports (the I/O half of a ports-and-adapters seam); static-content (hand-authored data arrays).
exclude: EDIT: replace the three examples below with YOUR real I/O-glue files (see the //exclusion-rule note above). This string itself matches nothing; delete it once you have your own list.
